concepts.definition: A morphism is an arrow in a category; exact formal properties depend on the category.
Composition combines composable morphisms, with order conventions determined by notation.
A composition convention that presents the first operation before the next operation.
The operation commonly written >>=, combining a monadic value with a function returning a monadic value.
A language-tagged string used to name or refer to a concept; preferred, alternative, and hidden labels serve different presentation and retrieval roles.
A curated set of terms used consistently to describe, index, retrieve, or organize information; mappings between vocabularies require explicit relationship types.
A documented association between practitioner or community language and a formal vocabulary concept, preserving the source expression and the confidence and scope of the mapping.
A relationship between expressions with similar but not necessarily identical meaning; context and sense must be checked before treating them as interchangeable.
A set G with an associative binary operation, an identity element, and an inverse for every element.
The unique element e of a group with e·g = g·e = g for every element g.
For an element g, the unique element g⁻¹ with g·g⁻¹ = g⁻¹·g = e.
The operation · : G × G → G combining two elements; written multiplicatively, additively, or as composition depending on convention.
A subset H of a group G that is itself a group under the restricted operation (written H ≤ G).
A subgroup N with gNg⁻¹ = N for every g in G (written N ⊲ G); exactly the kernels of homomorphisms and the denominators of quotient groups.
For a normal subgroup N, the group G/N of cosets of N with operation induced from G.
A map φ: G → H with φ(ab) = φ(a)φ(b) for all a, b in G.
A bijective homomorphism; groups related by one (G ≅ H) have identical group structure.
A group whose operation commutes: ab = ba for all elements. 'Commutative group' is the same concept.
A homomorphism from G into the symmetry group of a set X; equivalently a map G × X → X compatible with the operation and identity (written G ↷ X).
The group of all structure-preserving bijections of an object or set under composition; for a set X, Sym(X).
The category whose objects are groups and whose morphisms are group homomorphisms.
For a homomorphism φ: G → H, ker φ = {g in G : φ(g) = e_H}; always a normal subgroup of G. It measures exactly what φ collapses — the loss of a lossy map.

A stance-indexed state of one entity under one frame: E^T (read as threat) or E^O (read as opportunity). A reading is a property of the pair (entity, frame), never of the entity alone. Default frame = house frame; a foreign frame's reading carries its index: E^T_f.

One entity holding both valence readings simultaneously: E^{T∧O}. The two readings are both true at once and neither discharges the other; the notation keeps both projections available (contrast a single-valence label, which collapses the pair to one reading).

κ_{T→O} : E^T ⇢ E^O — a morphism between valence readings of the SAME entity whose object-component is the identity (id_E): the operator changes the relationship/stance, not the entity. κ is not ≅: it is not invertible in-frame; the reverse conversion is a distinct operator κ' (escalation), never written κ⁻¹. Conversions compose by ∘ (pipelines), associatively — the (G, ∘) frame law. A conversion record MUST name ker κ: what the source reading held that the target reading drops.

The competitive-frame instance of κ_{T→O}: OSINT + recruiting outreach converts a threat-reading into an opportunity-reading of the same entity (assimilation, ¬ %-pay brokerage — κ carries no price term; it is a relational operator, not a transaction).
The claim was checked against the live record by the speaker's own read. Glyph of record in v2: the eye (v1's example row for this concept is superseded).

NOT_ESTABLISHED is a chat epistemic marker, NOT a value (owner caution 2026-11-04 19:41 PT). Usage boundary: it is never a data-of-record token — the compression N∅ is chat-only, barred from data contexts; ledgers · feeds · DBs keep schema nulls where a fact is not established.
A provenance artifact of record (run id, artifact id, SHA, comment id) backing a claim.
A frozen capture of state at a point in time (census/feed snapshot).
A state after which the artifact of record no longer changes for judging/scoring.
A judgment of record issued by the seat holding the frame (PASS / FAIL / findings).
A verdict whose owed action/proof has been discharged. Under the glyph cap (owner correction 2026-11-04) it holds NO standalone glyph: written as the composition ⚖ + chord dch.

The artifact conforms to the cited spec/record. Glyph shared with math isomorphism — distinction is by domain slot: in caveman register this is a conformance predicate, not an isomorphism claim (which stays proof-gated per the notation spec).
One-glyph liveness state: green live, red down, yellow degraded.
Work cannot proceed on the named dependency; the blocker is named beside the glyph.
The next move belongs to the owner; lanes do not proceed past this glyph on their own authority.
A task/order sent to a lane or seat (up-arrow out).

mappings.evidence_note: Label-level candidate inherited from Issue #320; domain review required.
Keep related rather than exact: typeclass/monadic semantics and ordinary composition differ.

The group operation IS composition in the one-object-category view of a group, and in Grp composition of homomorphisms is the same operation one level up. Order/direction conventions per the matrix composition rows (g ∘ f applies f first). Related, not a label synonym.

A group is a one-object category whose morphisms are its elements; the identity element e is its identity morphism (matrix table row 'Identity morphism/function': id_A, 1_A). Scope: the link holds for the categorical view only — e is an element, not an arrow between distinct objects.
Grp is a category; its morphisms are group homomorphisms by definition. Links the category_of_groups concept to the seeded category_theory domain; no equivalence asserted beyond the definitional one.

MONOID ADJACENCY FLAG (not equivalence): a group is a monoid with inverses; Haskell's Monoid typeclass (like Semigroup/Monoid in FP generally) has NO inverse law, so Monoid ≠ group. No monoid concept is seeded yet; this mapping exists only to record the adjacency and block any exact_match claim. Target is the nearest seeded Haskell concept, used as an anchor, not a semantic peer.

ker φ is always a normal subgroup of the domain, and every normal subgroup is a kernel (of the quotient map). First isomorphism theorem: G/ker φ ≅ im φ. Operational rule (fleet notation spec): lossy maps MUST name their kernel.

κ is a morphism in the category of readings over a fixed object E (slice over E): its object-component is id_E and its work is entirely in the arrow. Composition of conversions = morphism composition.

κ preserves the operator-side structure (pipelines compose: κ2 ∘ κ1 is a conversion) while acting as identity on the object — homomorphism-like on relationships, NOT a map between two entities. ker rule carries over: a lossy conversion names ker κ.

A frame acting on an entity's readings resembles a group action G ↷ X: the actor (frame/house) moves the state, the underlying entity is the fixed carrier. Valence readings = points of the acted-on set.

Same glyph, different slot: caveman-register ≅ = conformance predicate (no proof owed); math-register ≅ = isomorphism claim, proof-gated (house notation spec: ≅ only where a proof discharges it, else ≈). Register determines which rule binds.
⚖✓ is ⚖ plus discharge: same judgment, its owed action closed. Composition of glyphs mirrors composition of states.
